How much does Depop actually take per sale?

"Depop takes 10%" and "Depop is free now" are both half-true, and which half depends on where the seller is. Depop runs three schedules at once: a 0% selling fee plus a separate payment-processing fee for US and UK sellers, and an older flat 10% selling fee everywhere else. Below is the same $50 sale priced under all three, plus what shipping and a Boosted Listing change.

The same $50 sale, three regions, no shipping

RegionSelling feeProcessing feePayoutEffective rate
United States$0.00 (0%)$2.10 (3.3% + $0.45)$47.904.2%
United Kingdom£0.00 (0%)£1.75 (2.9% + £0.30)£48.253.5%
Rest of world$5.00 (flat 10%)$0.00 (none broken out)$45.0010.0%

Same item, same price, three different payouts. A US or UK seller who still budgets for the old flat 10% is overestimating their fee by more than half; a rest-of-world seller reading a "0% selling fee" headline meant for US/UK sellers would badly underestimate theirs.

Worked example: shipping counts toward the processing base

A $22 item with $8 buyer-paid shipping, US region. Processing is charged on the item price plus shipping, not the item price alone.

LineAmount
Item price$22.00
Buyer-paid shipping$8.00
Processing base (item + shipping)$30.00
Processing fee (3.3% of $30 + $0.45)$1.44
Payout$28.56

Effective rate on the combined base: 4.8% -- higher than the 4.2% the no-shipping example above showed, because shipping is part of what the processing percentage applies to. Charging more for shipping does not dodge the fee -- it changes the base the fee is charged on.

Worked example: a Boosted Listing, same $50 US sale

Boosted Listings add 12% of the item price alone (not shipping), on top of the region's normal fee, and only on a sale that happened while the listing was boosted.

LineAmount
Item price$50.00
Processing fee (3.3% of $50 + $0.45)$2.10
Boost fee (12% of $50)$6.00
Total fees$8.10
Payout$41.90

Effective rate: 16.2%, versus 4.2% on the same sale unboosted. Depop's buyer-paid Marketplace fee (up to 5% + $1) is separate again -- it comes out of what the buyer pays at checkout, never out of this payout, and Depop has not published its sliding scale precisely enough to compute a figure for it here.

Do this with your own sale

The Depop fee calculator runs this same arithmetic on your own item price, shipping, item cost, and packaging cost, across all three regions, and solves backwards for the price that hits a target profit. Nothing you type leaves your browser.

Common questions

How much does Depop take on a $50 sale?

It depends entirely on the seller's region. A US seller pays a 0% selling fee plus $2.10 processing (3.3% of $50 + $0.45) and keeps $47.90 -- 4.2% effective. A UK seller pays 0% selling fee plus £1.75 processing (2.9% of £50 + £0.30) and keeps £48.25 -- 3.5% effective. A rest-of-world seller pays Depop's older flat 10% selling fee, $5.00, and keeps $45.00 -- exactly 10%, with no processing fee broken out separately.

Is Depop's 0% selling fee actually free?

No. The 0% figure describes only the selling fee. US and UK sellers still pay a separate payment-processing fee -- 3.3% + $0.45 in the US, 2.9% + £0.30 in the UK -- on the item price plus any shipping the buyer paid. On a $50 sale with no shipping that is $2.10, a 4.2% effective rate. "0% selling fee" and "free to sell" are not the same claim.

Does the processing fee apply to shipping too?

Yes. Depop's processing fee is charged on the item price plus buyer-paid shipping combined, not the item price alone. A $22 item with $8 buyer-paid shipping in the US pays processing on the full $30 base -- $1.44 -- not on $22 alone.

How much does a Boosted Listing add to the fee?

An extra 12% of the item price alone (not shipping), charged only on a sale that went through while the listing was boosted. On the same $50 US sale, that adds $6.00 on top of the $2.10 processing fee -- $8.10 total, 16.2% effective, versus 4.2% unboosted.

Rates change -- verify every figure against your own Depop payout statement before you price a listing. US and UK sellers pay a 0% selling fee, but a separate payment-processing fee (3.3% + $0.45 in the US, 2.9% + £0.30 in the UK) still comes out of the item price plus any shipping the buyer paid. Outside the US and UK, Depop's older flat 10% selling fee still applies. See your real payout, the price that hits a profit target, and how the same sale would pay out in all three regions.

Sellers outside the US and UK still run Depop's older flat 10% selling fee on the item price plus shipping, with no separate processing fee.

      Is Depop really free to sell on now?

      No. The 0% figure is only the selling fee. A separate payment-processing fee (3.3%+$0.45 in the US, 2.9%+£0.30 in the UK) still comes out of every sale, so a typical sale still pays a few percent in total — just less than the old flat 10%, and calculated differently.

      Does Depop's buyer Marketplace fee come out of my payout?

      No. Depop charges the buyer a separate Marketplace fee at checkout (up to 5% + $1 of the item and shipping cost, on a sliding scale Depop has not published in full). It is added to what the buyer pays on top of your price and never reduces what the seller receives.

      How much extra does a Boosted Listing sale cost?

      Depop charges an additional 12% fee, on the item price, on any sale that happened while the listing was boosted — on top of the normal regional selling and processing fees.

vs-tracking-depop-sales-in-a-spreadsheet.text:
← Depop fee calculator

Depop Fee Calculator vs. tracking Depop sales in a spreadsheet

A seller who prices more than one Depop sale usually ends up with a spreadsheet: a cell for the US or UK processing rate, a second set for the rest-of-world flat 10% schedule in case a listing sells to a different region, and a Boosted Listings row for the sales that were boosted. Each formula is ordinary arithmetic, copied from Depop's own Help Centre article. Keeping three regional schedules and a surcharge straight, and rebuilding the target-profit formula each time a rate changes, is the part that gets skipped when a sale needs a price today.

What each approach actually does

A spreadsheet can reproduce every rate this calculator applies — the US 3.3% + $0.45 processing fee, the UK 2.9% + £0.30 processing fee, the rest-of-world flat 10% selling fee, and the 12% Boosted Listings surcharge. Building it means opening Depop's Help Centre article, typing the right rate into the right cell for the region you sell into, and writing your own formula to solve backwards for the price that hits a target profit. It also means noticing, on your own, when Depop updates a rate.

This calculator keeps all three regional schedules and the Boosted surcharge on one screen, already wired to Depop's published figures, so a US sale, a UK sale, and a rest-of-world sale are the same worksheet instead of three separate ones. It solves backwards for the price that hits your target profit without a formula you have to write, and its region-compare table shows what the same sale would pay out in all three schedules with one click — useful when you are not certain which schedule your own account runs.

QuestionWhere to answer it

Common questions

Can a spreadsheet do this math instead?

Yes. The US/UK 0%-selling-fee-plus-processing schedule, the rest-of-world flat 10% schedule, and the 12% Boosted Listings surcharge are each ordinary arithmetic. Building it means typing Depop's published rates from its Help Centre into the right cells, then adding a formula that backs into a target-profit price and another set of cells if you ever sell in more than one region.

What does a spreadsheet not do that this calculator does?

Keep all three regional schedules and the Boosted surcharge on one screen, already wired to Depop's published rates, so a sale in any region is the same worksheet instead of three. It also solves backwards for the item price that hits a target profit without you writing that formula, and shows all three regions' payout for the same sale side by side with one click.

Is a spreadsheet ever the better choice?

Yes, when your situation has a wrinkle this calculator does not model — a bundle of several items in one Depop sale, a promotional credit, or a fee structure Depop has changed since this tool's rates were last checked against its Help Centre. A spreadsheet you build and update yourself can represent any rule you can describe. This calculator trades that flexibility for a form that already has the right fields for one item moving through one of Depop's three published schedules.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The calculator runs entirely in your browser. Item prices, costs, and payouts are never uploaded, and the optional usage counter records only which features were used and the day, never your numbers.
